digest.component_or_area: snapshot janitor / review-bot root disk management
propositions: The snapshot janitor's free-space reclaim trigger uses an absolute 2 GiB floor that is disk-size-blind, crossing only at 93.3% used on a 30 GiB volume—above the 85% alarm floor and unreachable during the incident.
The janitor's 7-day cold-trim exceeds container lifetime; the byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 is absent from _gc_pass, leaving only the absolute watermark as an active trigger.
Runtime injection of free-space values on a 30 GiB volume confirms zero evictions at 4.5 GiB free (85% used) and 3.0 GiB free (90% used), with first eviction only past the 93.3% threshold.

The fix adds a volume-relative headroom term (free_watermark_pct) that is the larger of the absolute floor and a percentage of total volume, with hysteresis reclaiming to a 5-point higher target to prevent re-firing.

The new knob defaults to 0 (off) for backward compatibility; the review-bot service sets it to 20 to reclaim at 80% used, matching autodeploy.sh's DISK_PRESSURE_PCT threshold and sitting below the 85% alarm floor.
Clamping free_watermark_pct to a maximum of 50% prevents footgun configurations where the trigger would demand the entire volume be free or exceed disk capacity.
